# Fallback glyph correction references

`fallback_correction_mathjax_3_2_2.json` contains 704 complete SVGs from D2's
unmodified MathJax 3.2.2 component, corresponding to MathJax source commit
`ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee`. Every expression is rendered in a
fresh VM, in both inline and display mode. The 352 display measurements are
rounded up from the original SVG's ex dimensions at 8 pixels per ex; none of
the expected SVGs or dimensions is generated by Go.

The generator verifies all three frozen asset SHA256 hashes before rendering:

| Asset | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| polyfills.js | 7fe1d048c78b0e09854c1259f7413868a51cc8f0c822489eb1ac36ae6c85ce01 |
| mathjax.js | cbbc1051a1f8abb1a181b6aa0fe927c020e3631ca630d19f52d9abb65b5ee869 |
| setup.js | a52cb0bbabfbd7796b9fedd793b9386c474e3123e788ee151cbe47ca1fa6e881 |

Regenerate with:

```sh
node --jitless testdata/generate_fallback_correction.cjs /path/to/pinned-assets
```

`CommonTextNodeMixin.computeBBox` in `ts/output/common/Wrappers/TextNode.ts`
assigns the current character's italic correction and skew on every loop
iteration, including when that character needs unknown-text measurement.
The Go fallback path retained the preceding known glyph's corrections. Clearing
those corrections restores the source behavior. The normal known-glyph path
still restores its own correction when a known glyph follows unknown text.

The 228 exact examples retained from the initial public macro corpus exercise
script, calligraphic, italic and upright text, accents, scripts, fractions,
boxes and font sizes. A further 464 public `mmlToken` examples keep compound
text within one TextNode: mi, mn, mo and mtext, italic and script variants,
known/unknown ordering, repeated fallback glyphs, numeric characters, CJK and
supplementary-plane CJK. Accents check skew, scripts check italic correction,
and known-after-unknown inputs verify that later glyph corrections return.
Twelve explicit-font controls exercise the unchanged measurement branch and
bring the total to 704.

All 704 complete SVGs and 352 display measurements pass after the correction.
The clean baseline `c7e6fda2f7595ddc7774b44449882a72d1335880` fails 76 of these
SVG comparisons. The remaining references are controls. An independent review
also compared 651 fresh public expressions across 13 variants, including
Japanese, Hangul, numeric text and explicit fonts, and found no regressions.

## Preserved unresolved parser examples

The initial 288-example corpus included 60 `mathit` examples containing a
snowman, such as `\mathit{f☃}`. They have an existing TeXAtom grouping mismatch
between the Go TeX parser and original MathJax, as well as an existing missing
italic fallback CSS attribute for the internal `-tex-mathit` variant. Their full SVGs remain in
`fallback_correction_residuals_mathjax_3_2_2.json`, together with the input,
original SVG, baseline SVG and current SVG. For all 60, the current SVG is
byte-identical to the baseline SVG and differs from the original. They are
recorded as unresolved evidence, not accepted as golden output or counted as
passing references. The generator explicitly retains this input inventory;
it does not filter cases based on whether Go passes.

`\mmlToken{mi}[mathvariant="italic"]{f☃}` and the corresponding mn/mo/mtext
controls are valid public TeX that isolate the renderer correction while the
separate parser issue remains unresolved. The generator refreshes the original
side of the residual file but deliberately preserves its historical Go
snapshots. A future parser fix should compare against those originals.

The independent review also encountered the already-existing fallback font
selection for the internal `-tex-calligraphic` and `-tex-mathit` variants.
Their geometry improves with this correction, but their fallback CSS remains
a separate issue. This change does not classify those full SVGs as exact.
